title: Bright & Cute - A Casual Game Music Pack - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track casual game score in one bright voice: menus, 8 levels with hurry up twins, shop, combos. MIDI + OGG.
description:
Bright & Cute is a 44 track score for casual, puzzle and match 3 games: the title, the menu, the level map, eight level themes, the shop, the idle screen, the pause, the results, the bonus round and the short cues a casual game fires all day. One bright voice from the first screen to the last.

One bright voice, checked on the shipped MIDI. Every track is in a major key or a major family mode (Ionian, Lydian or Mixolydian), and no part in any of the 44 tracks ever plays the minor third of its key: 9786 notes read, none of them that note. Even the Oops! and Time's Up cues stay major and get their sadness from a falling line instead. We ran the same check over our 22 other albums: none of them passes it on every track.

Hurry up twins. Each of the eight level themes comes with a twin: the same lead melody note for note, in the same key, about a quarter faster, over a busier band. Swap to it when the timer runs low. Both files have the same number of bars, so bar 5 of a level is bar 5 of its twin, and the Readme gives the arithmetic for swapping mid tune (Sugar Meadow: 10.0 seconds into the level is 8.0 seconds into the twin). Checked on the shipped MIDI for every pair.

What is in it. 32 full pieces and 12 short cues, 35:18 of music. Front door: Hello, Sunshine!, Press Start, Pick a Level and First Steps. Levels, each with its twin: Sugar Meadow (Sugar Meadow Hurry), Bubble Lagoon (Bubble Lagoon Hurry), Candy Clockwork (Candy Clockwork Hurry), Jelly Garden (Jelly Garden Hurry), Cloud Bakery (Cloud Bakery Hurry), Pebble Beach (Pebble Beach Hurry), Starlight Arcade (Starlight Arcade Hurry) and Lantern Fair (Lantern Fair Hurry). Between the levels: Penny Candy Store, Idle Afternoon, Tea Break, Score Tally, Bonus Round!, Prize Wheel, Big Cake Showdown, Daily Puzzle, Festival Weekend, Cozy Corner, Sticker Album and Thanks for Playing. Cues: Ready, Go!, Level Clear!, Oops!, Combo!, Super Combo!, Coin, Three Stars, Unlocked, Level Up, Time's Up, New Best! and Daily Gift.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 32 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read. 44 editable .mid sources. A Readme with per engine import notes and the twin swap formula, both proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

One family of five cells from one seed. Pop, Bloop, Hop, Twinkle and Droop. Pop opens every level; Bloop is Pop upside down and runs the menus and the shop; Hop moves only by step and gets you around; Twinkle opens out for the rewards; Droop falls by step for the small sad moments. 1312 statements and fragments of those cells across the album, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI.

Gate results. 776 theory checks and 492 audio checks, 0 failed, and both reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Three full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: Hello, Sunshine!, the title theme, and Sugar Meadow with Sugar Meadow Hurry, one level and its twin, so you can hear the swap back to back.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.title: Bright & Cute is out: a 44 track casual game score with hurry up twins
devlog.body:
Bright & Cute is a 44 track score for casual, puzzle and match 3 games: menus, a level map, eight level themes, a shop, an idle screen, results, a bonus round and the short cues for combos, coins, stars, wins and losses. It is live now, with three full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. A casual game shows the same few screens for hours, so its music has to stay cheerful without turning into a pile of unrelated jingles. Every track here is in a major key or a major family mode, and no part of any track ever plays the minor third of its key. That is checked note by note on the shipped MIDI, 9786 notes in all. The sad moments, like Oops! and Time's Up, fall by step instead of turning minor.

Hurry up twins. Each level theme has a twin with the same lead melody note for note, in the same key, about a quarter faster over a busier band, and the same number of bars. Swap when the timer runs low; the Readme gives the arithmetic for swapping mid tune.

How it was checked. 776 theory checks and 492 audio checks, 0 failed, with both reports inside the download. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks (Hello, Sunshine!, Sugar Meadow and Sugar Meadow Hurry) are for.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
